headline: Powerful earthquake leaves villages cut off

sources.title: Rescuers struggle to reach Colombia earthquake epicenter (CNN)
Colombia earthquake 2026: What you need to know (CARE)
Colombia rescue efforts press on after deadly earthquake (video, France 24 English)

chunks.text: Just after [[dawn]] on August 10, the ground in western Colombia began to shake. The earthquake, with a [[magnitude]] of 7.4, was one of the strongest in the country's modern history. People {{rushed out}} of their homes in cities as far away as Bogota and Medellin, and the [[shaking]] was felt in Ecuador and Panama. In several cities, buildings {{came down}}, and more than 290 people [[lost their lives]].

verbs.correct: To leave a place very fast
verbs.wrong: To lock the doors and hide
verbs.why: Rush out means to leave a building or a place very quickly, often because of danger. People rushed out of their homes the moment the ground began to shake.

verbs.wrong: To shake from side to side
verbs.why: Come down describes something falling from a higher position, like a wall or a roof collapsing. Several buildings came down when the earthquake struck.

chunks.text: The worst problems are in Choco, a [[region]] of mountains and deep forest near the [[epicenter]]. The quake {{set off}} [[landslides]] that [[buried]] the roads, and some villages were completely {{cut off}}: no cars, no trucks, no help. [[Rescue teams]] are trying to {{get through}} to them, but with the roads gone, even reaching the smallest towns can take days. Helicopters may be the only [[way in]].

verbs.why: Set off means to cause a chain of events to start suddenly. The quake set off landslides that buried the roads leading into the mountains.
Cut off means a place loses every connection to the outside world. Landslides left several mountain villages cut off, with no cars or trucks able to reach them.
Get through means to succeed in reaching a place that is hard to access. Rescue teams are trying to get through to villages the landslides blocked.

chunks.text: Closer to the cities, the rescue work never stops. Neighbors and [[firefighters]] {{dug out}} [[survivors]] from under fallen walls with [[bare hands]] and [[shovels]]. Rescuers work [[day and night]] and refuse to {{give up}} while people are still missing. Every person pulled from the [[rubble]] brings new energy to the teams.

verbs.correct: To free someone from under things
verbs.wrong: To carry someone to a doctor
verbs.why: Dig out means to free a person trapped under fallen rubble or debris. Neighbors and firefighters dug out survivors with nothing but bare hands and shovels.
Give up means to stop trying and quit. Rescuers refuse to give up while even one person is still missing under the rubble.

chunks.text: The government {{stepped in}} within hours and declared a [[state of emergency]]. [[Aid workers]] {{hand out}} clean water, food, and [[blankets]], and neighbors share what little they have. More than 140 people are still [[missing]], so [[officials]] fear the number of dead may {{go up}}. Many families lost everything and must now {{start over}} and slowly [[rebuild]] their lives. For them, the rescue workers who keep arriving are a reason to hope.

verbs.correct: To act to help in a problem
verbs.why: Step in means to take action and help when a problem needs a quick response. The government stepped in within hours and declared a state of emergency.

verbs.correct: To give things to many people
verbs.wrong: To sell things at low prices
verbs.why: Hand out means to give the same thing to many people at once. Aid workers hand out clean water, food, and blankets to families who lost everything.
Go up means a number rises, often about something you wish would stay low. Officials fear the number of dead may go up as more people are found.
Start over means to begin again from nothing after losing everything. Many families here must start over and slowly rebuild their homes and their lives.

mainIdea.s: A powerful earthquake hit western Colombia, and landslides left mountain villages cut off. Rescuers are working day and night to reach and free survivors.
mainIdea.why: The magnitude 7.4 quake killed more than 290 people, buried roads in Choco, and rescue teams are still trying to get through.

mainIdea.s: A powerful earthquake shook Colombia, but the rescue work is already finished. Roads reopened within a day, and every missing person has now been found safe.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the rescue is far from finished. Villages are still cut off, and more than 140 people are missing.

mainIdea.s: Colombia has opened a national center that teaches families how to prepare for earthquakes. Visitors practice safety drills inside a special shaking room.
mainIdea.why: The article is about a real earthquake and the rescue effort, not about a safety training center.
